People have always dressed according to class. Always. The difference between now and historically is that clothing is cheaper, readily available off the rack and produced cheaply and quickly.

Textiles used to be very expensive. Prior to the industrial revolution, cloth was made by hand weaving. This was time consuming and laborious. Most people only had one good set of clothing and their everyday clothing, of which they generally only had one or two "outer clothing" outfits. They only washed and changed their underclothing, of made of linen. People were often judged by the quality and whiteness of their linen.

Clothing was so expensive, that courtiers at Versailles literally bankrupted themselves with clothing. Granted, they often consisted of handmade laces, silks and solid gold buttons.

Even as late as the 50's, men often had only two or three suits and women two or three dresses, then their "Sunday best", for special occasions. Women's dresses often cost upwards of $400 a piece, in '50's money, so they lasted years and years and were well cared for. That's why you can still find them in consignment shops in good shape today. They were also tailor made to each unique buyer, so clothing generally fit your proportions exactly.

Enter in "ready to wear", and that changed everything. Nothing is tailor made anymore, unless you're wealthy or willing to invest in high quality items that you pay to have tailored. So, class dressing was, is and likely always will be a thing.
